question: Can a fixed Kontrol/KEVM environment initialize its Haskell backend and complete a machine proof about actual verifier code, after EXP-02 stopped before proof execution?
baseline: EXP-02 uses the pinned Kontrol v1.0.255 image digest sha256:858f004144d61b005997f56bb8b7cd15673850286c96e0e5ec0502d9c9a9e204. The first build hit cgroup OOM; sequential compilation passed that point but Kore definition validation failed without diagnostics. No formal claim was run.
method: Inspect available host and container runtimes, native Linux availability, effective VM memory and the pinned image without changing global Docker memory settings.

On the pinned image, isolate whether kore-exec can run a minimal documented command and can validate the previously generated actual definition; capture exit status, stdout/stderr, cgroup memory and version.

Only after backend validation succeeds with adequate measured resources, build a target linked to revised verifier source and bytecode, then execute one small property with its exact preconditions and logs.

When the previously compiled K definition proves generic and validates with an experiment-owned tmpfs, prepare a separate Foundry root from byte-identical revised Solidity source, compile with pinned solc 0.4.19, and attempt a small claim by reusing that exact validated definition without a full K rebuild. Record both revised source and bytecode hashes; stop if the definition is not reusable.

decision.successfulProof: A claim about the pinned actual verifier source or compiled bytecode completes, with version, code hash, assumptions, solver result and replay command recorded; this is only a slice of FV-03.
decision.toolFailure: Backend fails before a claim with a confirmed tool/runtime error; record the evidence and keep the requirement unverified.
decision.resourceFailure: OOM, effective memory below the gate, or timeout; record resource evidence and keep the requirement unverified.
decision.counterexample: A completed claim returns a concrete counterexample under its stated preconditions; record it separately from tool failure.
notAllowedAsSuccess: Assuming the verifier as a trusted black box
decision.sliceScope: The old source slice can establish tool execution only. The revised source and compiled bytecode require their own claim result. Neither slice establishes full FV-03.

record: Write new logs and JSON summaries under experiments/design/formal/ with distinct names. Preserve EXP-02 evidence and avoid creating a new Markdown file.
